claims.statement: CARE-SVD reduces mean absolute error to 0.623 +- 0.006 versus 0.851 +- 0.000 for majority-vote aggregation on UltraFeedback, a 26.8% error reduction (Table 1).
assumptions: 11-20 LLM judges scoring 0-10, per Appendix E.4
gamma_n tuned on a 15% validation split over the grid in Appendix E.3

claims.status_of_empirical_half: BLOCKED - the authors released no judge-score matrix for UltraFeedback; regenerating it needs GPU inference (Appendix E.2 reports an NVIDIA A100, up to 3 h per dataset). This campaign is CPU-only by authorisation.

claims.statement: CARE achieves an average 17.37% improvement over simple averaging across continuous-scoring benchmarks (Table 1).
claims.anchor: Section 5.1: 'Averaged across scoring datasets, CARE-SVD yields a 17.37% relative improvement over AVG and a 12.75% improvement over MV.'

machine_checkable_contract.definition_identification: enumerate candidate definitions of 'average relative improvement' and identify which reproduces BOTH 17.37% and 12.75% from Table 1 in exact rational arithmetic
machine_checkable_contract.empirical: reproduce the AVG and CARE-SVD MAE entries of Table 1 for every scoring dataset
machine_checkable_contract.unit_invariance: SCOPE QUALIFICATION established if, when ASSET's (MV, AVG, CARE-SVD) triple is rescaled by c: (a) the pooled mean-MAE ratio equals a baseline-MAE-weighted mean of per-dataset improvements as an exact identity, (b) the pooled statistic moves by more than 1 pp across c, (c) the unweighted across-benchmark average is exactly invariant, (d) the AVG-vs-MV ordering flips for some c, and (e) the unweighted average differs from 17.37 by more than 1 pp. This element CANNOT falsify the claim and an earlier revision of this file wrongly said it could: condition (c) holds by algebra -- (c*a - c*k)/(c*a) = (a - k)/a -- so the unweighted mean is unit-invariant identically, and (a) is likewise an identity. What the element establishes is the SIZE and DIRECTION of the weighting, which is not predictable from the algebra, and that is a qualification on the scope of a correctly reported number, not an error in it. The published verdict is VERIFIED with a quantified scope qualification; the field the code sets is `scope_qualification_established`.

claims.statement: On classification/preference datasets, CARE attains the best accuracy on 5 of 6 datasets, including a 13.4% relative improvement over the baseline on Summarize (0.814 +- 0.001 vs 0.705 +- 0.000) (Table 2).

machine_checkable_contract.structural: recompute the per-column argmax over all nine Table 2 methods; assert CARE wins exactly 5 of 6 and that CARE-Tensor leads on PKU-BETTER, SHP and Summarize
machine_checkable_contract.literal_generated_pair: FALSIFIED iff exact rational arithmetic gives abs((0.814 - 0.705)/0.705*100 - 13.4) > 0.05 percentage points
machine_checkable_contract.repair_control: replacing only 0.705 with the actual strongest Summarize baseline 0.718 must recover 13.4 within 0.05 percentage points
machine_checkable_contract.empirical: reproduce the CivilComments and PKU-BETTER columns from the authors' judge-score matrices, all nine methods, five seeds

claims.literal_verdict: FALSIFIED: the explicit pair gives 15.4609929%, not 13.4%; the nearby paper prose is correct only with GLAD at 0.718, which gives 13.3704735%.
claims.note: The generated challenge claim, not a paraphrase of the nearby paper prose, is authoritative. Both readings are decided explicitly and independently.
claims.status_of_empirical_half: PARTIAL - of Table 2's six columns, only CivilComments can be reproduced. Four have no released judge outputs (GPU-blocked, Appendix E.2). PKU-BETTER has judge outputs but its released labels are constant, so it is BLOCKED by a failed integrity precondition, not scored.
integrity_preconditions: the dataset's released gold labels must have >= 2 distinct values and a minority class >= 1%; a dataset failing this is BLOCKED, never FALSIFIED

claims.statement: Proposition 4.1 establishes identifiability of latent-judge directions up to sign and permutation under shared confounders, with perturbation stability bounds (Section 4).
claims.anchor: Proposition 4.1 (Section 4); Assumptions D.1-D.2, Theorem D.3, Theorem D.4 (Appendix D.2)

assumptions_as_stated.main_text: K_HH = diag(d_1..d_h), d_1 > ... > d_h > 0; columns of K_JH ORTHOGONAL
assumptions_as_stated.appendix: K_HH^-1 = diag(lambda_1..lambda_h), lambda_1 > ... > lambda_h > 0; columns of K_JH ORTHONORMAL

machine_checkable_contract.identifiability: symbolic proof that L k_i = lambda_i k_i and rank(L - lambda_i I) = p - 1 for a parameterised family of orthonormal K
machine_checkable_contract.stability_constant: sup over E of ||u~_i - s u_i|| delta_i / (||K_HH^-1||_2 ||E||_2) <= 4
machine_checkable_contract.counterexample_search: construct K_JH, K'_JH satisfying every main-text hypothesis with the same L but columns not related by sign/permutation; and a family on which the main-text bound is violated by an unbounded factor

claims.statement: Theorem 4.2 gives a finite-sample convergence rate of O(sqrt(eta/n) * 1/(xi(T)*delta)) for the spectral estimation path (Section 4).
claims.anchor: Theorem 4.2 (Section 4) = Theorem D.5, proved in Appendix D.6 from Chandrasekaran et al. (2012) Thm 4.1 and Yu et al. (2015) Thm 2

machine_checkable_contract.literal_sign_counterexample: at exact recovery, choose the equally valid eigenvector -u; D.5's raw distance is 2 and its RHS is 0, while the sign-aligned control is 0
machine_checkable_contract.missing_zero_gap_family: for L*=2u1u1^T+a*uhuh^T and E=(a/r)(uhv^T+vuh^T), prove error/(||E||/delta_paper) diverges as a->0 while the ratio using delta_full=a stays bounded
machine_checkable_contract.minimum_signal_control: couple n=(r/a)^2 so a/sqrt(p/n)=r/sqrt(p); a fixed sufficiently large r meets any finite minimum-signal constant while the paper-gap violation still diverges
machine_checkable_contract.gaussian_two_point_lower_bound: construct two CARE-factorizable Gaussian models with weak eigenvectors separated by theta, n-sample KL bounded under n=(c/a)^2, and a Le Cam error-probability lower bound above D.5's failure budget while its paper-gap rate tends to zero
machine_checkable_contract.derivation: symbolically compose the two cited bounds and check they yield the stated rate and the stated n >= 8 C_1^2 eta /(xi^2 delta^2 alpha^2)
machine_checkable_contract.cited_constant: search for a symmetric perturbation violating ||u^ - u|| <= 2^{3/2}||Delta||_2/gap
machine_checkable_contract.calibrated_scaling: run the Algorithm-1 estimator and SEARCH for the smallest n reaching accuracy alpha; fit exponents of n*(alpha) and n*(delta) and compare with -2 and -2

claims.literal_verdict: FALSIFIED by the sign counterexample, the missing-zero-gap family, and a Gaussian two-point minimax lower bound that decides the statistical rate itself. The previous finite-grid sweeps are retained but do not carry the verdict.
claims.non_circularity: the formulation counterexamples are exact; the missing-gap result is symbolic in a, and the statistical lower bound is recomputed independently from the direct 2x2 Gaussian trace/log-determinant KL formula.

claims.statement: Theorem 4.3 gives a sample complexity bound n >~ sigma_max^6/(delta^2 pi_min^2) p log(p/eps) for recovering the mixture parameters (mu_qc, pi_qc) (Section 4).
claims.anchor: Theorem 4.3 (Section 4) = Theorem D.9, proved in Appendix D.6

machine_checkable_contract.derivation: compose the paper's own eq. (8), (10)-(12) and eq. (11) and compare each composed bound with the stated one
machine_checkable_contract.empirical: hold mu, pi, delta, p, eps fixed, scale sigma_max, set n at the theorem's own threshold, and measure max|pi^ - pi| against C_2 sqrt(p log(p/eps)/n)

falsification_criterion.pre_registered: the stated weight bound is violated if the measured error does not decay like sigma^-3 along the theorem's own sample-complexity boundary, since no fixed universal C_2 can then satisfy it for all sigma_max.

added_after_baseline.criterion: the stated p*log(p/eps) factor is falsified if, with sigma, delta and pi_min held fixed, the measured exponent of n* on p*log(p/eps) exceeds 1 by more than two standard errors under BOTH n* estimators
added_after_baseline.why_added: The pre-registered criterion tests only the sigma boundary. While repairing a censored search grid (every pi_min setting had returned n* = 5000, the grid floor) the p sweep became measurable for the first time and immediately exceeded its bound. The criterion was written before that sweep was re-run with the corrected grid, but AFTER the censored run had already shown a large p-exponent.
added_after_baseline.honest_status: POST-HOC. This is a post-hoc test, not a pre-registered one. The three admissibility gates it must clear (both n* estimators resolving and agreeing, the restart-budget attribution, and the constancy audit of every other quantity in the bound) were each written before their own outcomes were known, but the decision to test the p factor at all was prompted by seeing a large exponent.
